doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

chapter: Session stories and why he was hired
title: Playing the rock and roll guitar sound
summary: Bucky describes the high electric sound and the muffled wrist-muting technique used on rock dates.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Every one. Was there — do you remember any conversation about having to play different for the rock & roll dates?

Well we knew it was a different kind of sound. You had a guitar with a high pitch electric sound, real high. You knew how to do it. Sometimes we’d go on a date and we’d all make up a thing. One would do [scats] with your wrist on the strings, you get a real muffled sound. That was the most popular way of doing it.
